programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc:
Sa phrògram seo tha e a’ dol an sàs ann an cèic mheasan. Bha a sheanmhair a’ cleachdadh pùdar uighe anns a chèic aig àm san robh an Cuibhreannachadh dìreach air sgur, ach cha chuala Griogar guth riamh air!
A’ tadhal air nàbaidh a tha tric sa ghàrradh, cluinnidh e dè dh’ fhàsas ann am polytunnel ann an Leòdhas. A’ tilleadh dhachaidh le dòrlach lusan is eile, cuiridh e iad ri slisean bradain ann an sabhs geal.
Tha mìlsean carraigin san leabhar cuideachd, biadh feamad air an robh muinntir nan eilean riamh measail. Tha Griogar a’ dol gu cladach Bhràgair a choinneachadh ri fear a bhios ga bhuain, ‘s a dh’innseas dha mar a bhruicheas e e.
Gregor takes on a classic fruit cake. Written not long after rationing, Grannie’s recipe calls for powdered egg - a new experience for Gregor! He visits his neighbour, a keen gardener, to learn about the things you can grow in a polytunnel in Lewis. Returning home with a handful of tasty ingredients, he adds them to grannie’s recipe for salmon steaks with white sauce.
Another find in the book is carageen pudding. This traditional island dish uses seaweed, so Gregor visits the shore at Bragar to meet a local man who regularly gathers it on the rocks and has some handy tips for cooking with it. Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Taobh a-staigh a ballachan bha mac-talla binn, drùidhteach aig ùrnaighean is ceòl. O chionn ghoirid, bha a' chathair-eaglais gun ghuth - agus tha an t-àm ann a h-ath-bheothachadh.
Fhad 's a bha Notre-Dame a' losgadh, bha an t-saoghal air fad a' gal, 's a' cuimhneachadh air an laigse is am bàsmhorachd fhèin. Tha luchd-rannsachaidh a-nise ag amas air fuaimearrachd, solas agus dathan na cathair-eaglais ath-chruthachadh. Thathar a' glanadh còmhdach sùith bhon ghlainne-dhathte. Aig an dearbh àm, chithear fìor dhath na cloiche: tha fianais ann gun robh a' chathair-eaglais air a peantadh air fad. Tron fhilm seo tha saidheans a' frithealadh naomhachd. Le dòchas gun cluinnear fuaim an òrgain as ainmeil air thalamh a-rithist taobh a-staigh ballachan Notre-Dame.
Tha am prògram seo a' tarraing oidhirpean eòlaichean agus ìomhaighean iongantach dhen làrach-thogail ri chèile, agus a' taisbeanadh dè a tha a' dèanamh Notre-Dame na samhla air beatha is bòidhchead. Leanaidh sinn luchd-saidheans, eachdraichean agus ailtirean is iad ag obair còmhla ann an oidhirp an t-seud seo ath-nuadhachadh.
Within Notre-Dame's walls, prayers and music once resonated with emotion and beauty. But due to the blaze, the cathedral lost its voice - and it is time to bring it back to life. As Notre-Dame burned, the whole world wept as it was confronted to its own fragility. Researchers now aim to recover the cathedral's acoustics, light and colours that created its beauty.
A dense layer of soot is removed from the stained glass. Meanwhile, the stone - now exposed - reveals its true colors: we have proof that the cathedral was fully painted. Throughout this film, science serves the sacred. The hope is that the world's most famous organ will once again resound within Notre-Dame’s walls.
This documentary combines experts’ interventions and exclusive footage of the construction site, while unveiling what makes Notre-Dame a shrine of life and beauty. We observe scientists, historians and architects working together, preparing to restore this jewel of humanity.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Anna Murray Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Shona Henderson Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.sub-title: Brot Coiridh le Leantail is Leigeas ║ AiganTaighleE6/12
programme.desc:
'S e th' ann am Brot fìor bhlast' de Choiridh leantail, ach lòn sònraicht' nach dìochuimhnich thu ann an cabhaig.
An extremely delicious curried lentil soup is a special lunch which you won't forget in a hurry.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Abigail Maciver Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: OMC
programme.desc:
Sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters and spoofs. Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent.
Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker. Includes the latest updates from the ferry office, a recipe with a difference, and red hot passion finds physical expression via a clown love triangle.
Anns an ceithreamh prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho na sgriobhadariean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. Gheibh sinn an turas sa beachd car eadar-dhealaichte airson reasabaidh, tha cridhe Doodles an cleasaiche a’ briseadh agus, ’s e cheist as motha an t-seachdan sa, am bidh an aiseig a’ seòladh?
In Gaelic with English subtitles Various - Lana Pheutan Various - Hannah McKirdy Various - Darren MacLean Various - David Walker Various - Carina MacLeod Various - Iain Beggs Director - Fiann Macleod Producer - Marie McDonald Executive Producer - Rab Christie.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc:
Le ball-coise ann an Alba ann an staing le gainnead chluicheadairean òga a’ faighinn chothroman, tha an SFA airson crathadh a thoirt air na riaghailtean aca. Tha Calum MacIllinnein a’ rannsachadh nam planaichean, a’ coinneachadh ri clubaichean, cluicheadairean is luchd-leantainn, is a’ faighneachd dè thèid again air ionnsachadh bho shiostam Nirribhidh.
As Scottish football faces a crisis over its pipeline of talent, the SFA are planning an overhaul of youth development. Calum Maclennan examines the plans, meeting clubs, players and fans, and asks what we can learn from Norway’s system.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Sar Sgeoil
programme.desc:
Cathy Macdonald explores the fact behind the fiction in Mary Shelley's Frankenstein. From the resurrectionists and anatomy classes of the early 19th century to the sights and smells of the whaling ships coming into port, Cathy finds out where Mary took her inspiration for the book and how her time spent living in Dundee as a teenager helped to inspire the novel.
Cathy also visits Orkney, where Mary Shelley chose to take her famous character and his creature. Frankenstein - the story and the character - have endured over the centuries since it was published in 1818, inspiring numerous films, television shows and comics. Cathy talks to University of Dundee's Chair of Comic Studies about the impact the novel has had on the comic world. Cathy reveals the often unknown Scottish connections to one of the most famous novels ever written.
Tha Cathy Dhòmhnallach a’lorg na fìrinn air cùl na sgeòil anns an leabhar Frankenstein aig Màiri Shelley. Eadar gadaichean chorp dhaibhsan a bha sireadh eòlas-bodhaig, tràth san 19mh linn, gu seallaidhean is fàilidhean luing-seilge nam mucan mara a’tighinn gu cala – tha Cathy a’faighinn a-mach an iomadh rud a dhùisg mac-meanmna an ùghdair, nam measg an ùine a chuir i seachad ann an Dundè na deugair. Thèid Cathy cuairt gu Arcaibh, far an do chuir Màiri a caractar ainmeil gu eilean uaignidh.
Sheas an leabhar gu làidir bhon a nochd e an toiseach ann an 1818, le sruth de filmichean, prògraman TBh agus pàipeirean éibhinn ga leantail.
Bruidhnidh Cathy ris a Phroifeasar airson Eòlas Chomaigean ann an Dundè, mun bhuaidh a bh’aig an leabhar air irisean dealbhaichte atharrach.Bheir i gu aire an t-sluaigh an ceangal làidir ri Alba a th’aig leabhar cho ainmeil sa nochd riamh ann an clò.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Cathy MacDonald.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Tha na h-Abadas air a bhith trang a' togail caisteal-sneachd 's iad a-nis a' coimhead air n-adhart ri geama a chluich. 'S e Hari a tha a' lorg am facal an-diugh 's e am broinn an taighe.
After building a snow castle in the mountains, the Abadas settle down with Ben for the word game. Soon, Hari is sent to look for a stool inside the house.

programme.sub-title: Cath-Tharraing ║ Losgannan. S1E23/26. Tug of War ║ Losgannan. S1E23/26
programme.desc:

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc:
Tha Meanbh Chlangair 's a caraidean Lusach, a' cluich ceòl còmhla ris na Craobhan Ciùil. Dè tha siud? Tha cuideigin eile ri seinn cuideachd. Saoil cò th' ann?
Tiny Clanger and her flower friends are making music with the Music Trees. What’s that? Someone else is singing, too. Who could it be? Narrator - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc:
Tha Oona ‘s Otto a' cur romhpa a dhol a choimhead Leum a’ Bhradain ach mus fhaigh iad falbh, feumaidh Otto Pip ‘s Pop a chur dhan leabaidh às-dèidh an t-sealg-oidhch'. Ge-tà, chan eil e coltach g’ eil na cailleachan-oidhche bheaga idir sgìth.
Oona and Otto decide to spend the morning watching the 'salmon leap' but before they can set off, Otto must put Pip and Pop to bed after the night hunt. Unfortunately for Otto, it doesnt seem that the young owls are in the least bit tired. Aithris - John Carmichael Oona - Zoe Drysdale Baba/Pop - Adam Kaiess Otto - Oscar Donald Pip - Philippa Keenan Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean Singer - Zoe Drysdale.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc:
Tha farspach a’ nochdadh air a’ chreag agus i ann an sunnd airson mi-mhodh. Ge-tà, nuair a dh’fheuchas i ri biadh a ghoid bho fhaoileag bhìodach, tha Oona ‘s Baba a' tighinn na h-aghaidh gus an t-ìsean a dhìon!
The great gull has made her way to Puffin Rock and is intent on causing all sorts of mischief. However, when she sets her sights on a poor little seagul chick, Oona and Baba are ready to challenge her and protect the little bird! programme.sub-title: Cuir am Botal Mun Cuairt ║ S1E5/26. Spin the Bottle ║ S1E5/26
programme.desc: Plankton poses as a wish-granting genie. Tha Planctan a’ dol ann an riochd dìnidh a shàsaicheas mhiannan.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc:
Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd.
Our cameras are back at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche for a new term. A lot has happened over the holidays. The in-service day wasn’t as successful as Mr Mackle had hoped and Ms Sharpe has made the newspapers after what happened at the Mòd.

programme.title: Aidan: Balach Beag Muay Thai
programme.desc:
Tha Aidan, a tha deich bliadhna a dh’aois, ag ullachadh airson an t-sabaid às mòtha de bheatha ’s e a’ gabhail pàirt ann an Farpais WBC Muay Thai na Cruinne. Na dhùthaich fhein, Alba, tha fios aige gu bheil e math air sabaid Muay Thai ach ciamar a thèid dha an aghaidh clann bho dùthchannan a tha tòrr nas mòtha? Tha sinn dha leantainn, ag obair gu cruaidh air na sgilean Muay Thai aige, an cois a neach-teagaisg – a mhàthair. Cuideachd, chì sinn mar a tha e ag obair a dh’ionnsaidh a bhith làidir gu leòr airson an fharpais air fad. Cluinnidh sinn bho Aidan ciamar a tha e dol a dheiligeadh ri bhith sabaid an aghaidh clann a dh’fhadaodh a bhith suas ri 35cg, ’s gun esan ach 29cg. Dè sèorsa buaidh a bheir seo air na sabaidean aige?
Aidan, a ten-year-old boy from Scotland, prepares for the biggest fight of his life as he competes in the WBC World Muay Thai festival. In Scotland, he knows that he is a good Muay Thai fighter, but how will he compare to children from much bigger countries?
We follow his journey as he practises his Muay Thai technique with his coach, who is also his mum, as well as working on building his endurance so he will be able to compete in multiple fights. Aidan also discusses his height as he will be competing in the under 35kg weight bracket. At 29kg, will Aidan’s small stature affect the outcome of his fights? Director - Nina Torrance Producer - Maureen MacLeod Producer - Annie Cheape Executive Producer - Phillis Fermer Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc:
Tha Sebastian cho toilicht’ nuair a tha e a’ faighinn seann leabhar-latha beanntan Chaspair – leabhar air leth sònraicht’. Gu mì-fhortanach ge-tà, tha Mgr. Turner ga thoirt bhuaithe, mar pheanas. Ciamar a gheibh e air seo innnse do Chaspair?
Sebastian is so happy when he gets Caspar’s old mountain journal, a very special book. Unfortunately, Mr Turner confiscates it as a punishment. How can he tell Caspar about this? Sebastian - Ellen Macdonald Adele - Mischa Macpherson Cameron - Claire Frances MacNeil Gabriel - Iona Davidson Caspar - Calum MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seonaidh
Shaun the Sheep
programme.sub-title: An Spleuchd ║ Seonaidh. S4E25/30. The Stare ║ Seonaidh. S4E25/30
programme.desc:
Tha Bitzer air fois fhaighinn agus Seonaidh bochd fo gheasaibh aig Mowermouth an Gobhair. Ge-tà leis an treud air fad fo smachd Mowermouth, tha Bitzer a' tuigse gu bheil feum aige air a dheagh charaid.
Bitzer gets his wish for some peace and quiet when Shaun becomes hypnotised by Mowermouth the goat and finally stops bothering him. But with the whole flock under the influence of Mowermouth's powerful gaze, Bitzer soon realises just how much he needs his old buddy.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo explores Benmore Botanic Garden near Dunoon in Argyll. He visits the Victorian fernery, the Tasmanian Ridge and the Chilean Rainforest Glade where he plants a monkey puzzle tree.
Dr Mark Newman of the Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh, tells us about the important role of botanic gardens in conservation and education.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’gabhail chuairt tro Ghàrradh Luibheanach na Beinne Mòire faisg air Dùn Omhain ann an Earra-Ghaidheal. Tha e a’faicinn a’chruinneachadh rainich, a thòisich san naoitheamh linn deug, agus chì e earrainn den ghàrradh an riochd Tasmania agus cuideachd ceò-choille Chile, far a bheil e fhèin a’cur craobh monkey-puzzle.
Innsidh an t-Oll. Mark Newman bho Ghàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn-Èidinn dhuinn cho cudromach sa tha gàrraidhean luibheanach a thaobh glèidhteachas agus foghlam.

programme.title: Na Boireannaich a Thog Glasgow City
programme.desc:
Denied a pathway to football as children, this is the inspiring journey of Carol Anne Stewart and Laura Montgomery, the formidable duo who had a vision of creating sporting opportunities for women and girls in Scotland. They founded Glasgow City FC in 1998 with aspirations to become a dominant force in Scottish football and a strong contender in Europe. They delivered, creating Scotland’s most successful women’s football team, winning 13 League titles in succession and reaching Uefa's Women’s Champions League quarter-finals twice. Sustaining their legacy is the club’s thriving academy, enabling girls to follow their footballing dreams.
Le slighe gu dreuchd ball-coise air a dhiùlt dhaibh an uair a bha iad nan cloinn, tha Na Boireannaich a Thog Glasgow City ag innse sgeulachd Carol Anne Stewart agus Laura Montgomery, an dithis aig an robh an lèirsinn cothroman a chruthachadh airson boireannaich is clann-nighean ann an Alba. ’S iadsan a stèidhich Glasgow City FC ann an 1998 le amas tighinn am bàrr an Alba sa chumadh ceann a’ mhaide ris an clubaichean as motha san Roinn Eòrpa. Chan eil teagamh nach do shoirbhich leotha le trì deug tiotal an sreath a chèile a thuilleadh air a bhith a’ ruighinn cairteal cuairtean deireannach Champions League nam Ban dà thuras. Tha an Academaidh shoirbheachail aca a’ feuchainn ris an dìleab a chumail a’ dol, a’ toirt cothrom do nigheanan òga dreuchd a dheànamh dhaibh pèin ann am ball-coise.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Alex O'Henley Director - Margot McCuaig Executive Producer - Iseabail Mactaggart.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc:
’S caomh leinn a bhith smaoineachadh gu bheil eòlas againn air an t-saoghal timcheall oirnn, ach dè ma tha sinn dìreach a’ faicinn pàirt dheth? Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ toirt cuireadh dhuinn coiseachd, snàmh agus leum am measg nam beathaichean agus an saoghal aca a thuigsinn nan àrainneachd fhèin.
Thairis air ceithir eapasodan iongantach, tha sinn ag ionnsachadh mu chiad-fàthan cumhachdach nam beathaichean, bho fradharc buileach mionaideach gu iasg a tha a’ blasad len craiceann. Faic mar a tha tìgearan gan cleith fhèin le bhith a’ cleachdadh an dath orains, mar a tha leumadairean a’ seòladh a’ chuain le echo-location, mathain-nighe a’ dèanamh an slighe le spògan air leth faireachail, agus tha fiù ’s craobhan a’ cur a-mach rabhaidhean ceimigeach.
Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ taisbeanadh taobhan falaichte de nàdar - cailèideascop de chiad-fàthan nach eil sinn ach air tòiseachadh a’ tuigsinn.
We think we know the world around us, but what if we’re only seeing part of the picture? This series invites you to walk, swim or leap in someone else’s paws, fins or wings - and experience life from a wild perspective.
Across four mind-blowing episodes, we uncover animal super-senses, from high-resolution vision to fish that taste with their skin. Discover how tigers turn orange into camouflage, dolphins navigate the deep using echo-location, raccoons feel their way with hyper-sensitive paws, and even trees send out chemical alarms. This is the hidden side of nature - a kaleidoscope of sensations we’re only just beginning to understand.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Annella MacLeod Executive Producer - Alasdair Fraser Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Ceol Sith
programme.desc:
Thigibh air turas a-steach gu saoghal shìthichean agus creutairean os-nadarra eile. Air chuairt ann an Alba, tha Ingrid NicEunraig a’ cluinntinn beul-aithris agus sgeulachdan a tha fhathast beo. Anns a’ program sònraichte seo, tha Ingrid a’ tòiseachadh ann an Loch Abar far a bheil mòran stòraidhean mar seo air maireachdainn.
As dèidh sin tha I a’ cluinntinn sgeulachdan nas tradisteanta anns an Eilean Sgiathanach. Tha I cuideachd a’ cluinntinn sgeulachd bhampire ann an Glaschu agus mu bheathaichean bhon uisge ann an Uibhist, mu maighidinn-mara agus each-uisge. Tha a cuid-siubhal ga brosnachach gus ceòl ùr a sgriobhadh agus a chluich ann an cuid de na h-àiteachan as drùidhteach san dùthaich. Air aon làimh ’s eeàlachas a th’anns a’ phrògram seo ach aig an aon àm, tha e a’ toirt dhuinn sealladh air spiorad mac an duine.
This is a thrilling journey into the world of fairies and folklore. Ingrid Henderson presents a tour around Scotland’s rich mythical worlds and composes music to bring them back to life.
Ingrid starts on her home turf in Lochaber, where these stories are very much alive, and then heads to Skye with its traditional fairy stories. She also hears about a terrifying creature in Glasgow - the Gorbals vampire - and talks to people in Uist about watery creatures such as mermaids and kelpies.
As she travels, Ingrid draws inspiration from the stories to create and perform specially composed music for the programme in stunning locations around the country. On the one hand, this documentary is pure escapism, but it also gives us insight into the human spirit.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ingrid Henderson Executive Producer - Maureen MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - Annie Cheape.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.desc:

They’re one of the biggest seeds in the world – there's a record of one topping the scales at 25 kilos! – but as we know, bigger isn’t always better when it comes to our bidders...
Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?
Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.
With their verdicts in, Monica and Marcus must make the final call. For some chefs, the critics’ reactions could strengthen their case; for others, they could expose the smallest weaknesses. With only three places in knockout week up for grabs, who has done enough to stay in the competition, and whose MasterChef journey ends here? programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
A healthy young labourer is found dead in a shallow ornamental pond on the vast country estate of Lady Philippa Armstrong and her son Jonathan. While the tragic incident initially appears to be nothing more than a straightforward workplace accident, Rose and Raj are called in to investigate glaring discrepancies. After all, how does a strong young man manage to drown in mere inches of water?
Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.

programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: This City Is Ours

programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.

A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Tall Tales and Murder
programme.desc:
Bridget is an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin care home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges late-night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely.
Into this secret world comes Paul, a vulnerable young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker. Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so he calls on his guardian angel - an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan. Bunny uses his personal history with the matron of Bridget’s nursing home to pull in a favour - a favour that will cost him dear. On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together, a mysterious comatose patient known only as ‘Anonymous’ wakes up and reveals he is a long-lost gangster with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. Could this treasure be the answer to all of Bridget and Paul’s troubles? Will they risk everything to find it?

programme.title: US Midterm Elections 26
programme.desc:
Live from Washington DC, Clive Myrie, Sumi Somaskanda and Caitríona Perry guide viewers through a decisive night in American politics with far-reaching implications for the world. As polls close and votes pour in across the country, the balance of power in Washington is at stake.
Throughout the night, BBC News will bring viewers the latest results as they happen, along with expert analysis of the races, candidates and issues driving voters to the polls, from affordability and immigration to tariffs, international conflict and the growing impact of data centres on local communities.
With correspondents reporting from across the United States and the world, plus Ros Atkins at the touchscreen breaking down turnout, voting trends and the shifting balance of power, BBC News will track every major development in real time.

programme.desc:
First to show his wares to Simon Bower and Nigel Havers is Philip, who has come up from Stoke with a stake, some holy water and all the other accoutrements any budding vampire killer would need. It’s an unusual collection, so which of the dealers will bite?
Next through the doors is Ben, with a rare coco de mer seed from a palm tree that only grows on two islands in the Seychelles. They’re one of the biggest seeds in the world – there's a record of one topping the scales at 25 kilos! – but as we know, bigger isn’t always better when it comes to our bidders...
Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?
Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.
With their verdicts in, Monica and Marcus must make the final call. For some chefs, the critics’ reactions could strengthen their case; for others, they could expose the smallest weaknesses. With only three places in knockout week up for grabs, who has done enough to stay in the competition, and whose MasterChef journey ends here? Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
A healthy young labourer is found dead in a shallow ornamental pond on the vast country estate of Lady Philippa Armstrong and her son Jonathan. While the tragic incident initially appears to be nothing more than a straightforward workplace accident, Rose and Raj are called in to investigate glaring discrepancies. After all, how does a strong young man manage to drown in mere inches of water?
Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.
Struggling to navigate the complex social dynamics of the estate, Rose reluctantly accepts Joe’s persistent interference. Together, the duo soon uncover a dark web of deep-seated secrets and lies within the family and their devoted staff.

Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Paula, Ranie, Aaron and Pam – take on the Bridge of Lies.
One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game.
There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Tall Tales and Murder
programme.desc:
Bridget is an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin care home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges late-night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely.
Into this secret world comes Paul, a vulnerable young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker. Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so he calls on his guardian angel - an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan. Bunny uses his personal history with the matron of Bridget’s nursing home to pull in a favour - a favour that will cost him dear. On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together, a mysterious comatose patient known only as ‘Anonymous’ wakes up and reveals he is a long-lost gangster with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. Could this treasure be the answer to all of Bridget and Paul’s troubles? Will they risk everything to find it?

programme.title: US Midterm Elections 26
programme.desc:
Live from Washington DC, Clive Myrie, Sumi Somaskanda and Caitríona Perry guide viewers through a decisive night in American politics with far-reaching implications for the world. As polls close and votes pour in across the country, the balance of power in Washington is at stake.
Throughout the night, BBC News will bring viewers the latest results as they happen, along with expert analysis of the races, candidates and issues driving voters to the polls, from affordability and immigration to tariffs, international conflict and the growing impact of data centres on local communities.
With correspondents reporting from across the United States and the world, plus Ros Atkins at the touchscreen breaking down turnout, voting trends and the shifting balance of power, BBC News will track every major development in real time.

Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?

Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

While the tragic incident initially appears to be nothing more than a straightforward workplace accident, Rose and Raj are called in to investigate glaring discrepancies. After all, how does a strong young man manage to drown in mere inches of water?
Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.
Struggling to navigate the complex social dynamics of the estate, Rose reluctantly accepts Joe’s persistent interference. Together, the duo soon uncover a dark web of deep-seated secrets and lies within the family and their devoted staff.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.

programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there.
