programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Tall Tales and Murder
programme.desc:
Bridget is an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin care home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges late-night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely.
Into this secret world comes Paul, a vulnerable young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker. Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so he calls on his guardian angel - an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan. Bunny uses his personal history with the matron of Bridget’s nursing home to pull in a favour - a favour that will cost him dear. On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together, a mysterious comatose patient known only as ‘Anonymous’ wakes up and reveals he is a long-lost gangster with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. Could this treasure be the answer to all of Bridget and Paul’s troubles? Will they risk everything to find it?

programme.title: US Midterm Elections 26
programme.desc:
Live from Washington DC, Clive Myrie, Sumi Somaskanda and Caitríona Perry guide viewers through a decisive night in American politics with far-reaching implications for the world. As polls close and votes pour in across the country, the balance of power in Washington is at stake.
Throughout the night, BBC News will bring viewers the latest results as they happen, along with expert analysis of the races, candidates and issues driving voters to the polls, from affordability and immigration to tariffs, international conflict and the growing impact of data centres on local communities.
With correspondents reporting from across the United States and the world, plus Ros Atkins at the touchscreen breaking down turnout, voting trends and the shifting balance of power, BBC News will track every major development in real time.

programme.desc:
First to show his wares to Simon Bower and Nigel Havers is Philip, who has come up from Stoke with a stake, some holy water and all the other accoutrements any budding vampire killer would need. It’s an unusual collection, so which of the dealers will bite?
Next through the doors is Ben, with a rare coco de mer seed from a palm tree that only grows on two islands in the Seychelles. They’re one of the biggest seeds in the world – there's a record of one topping the scales at 25 kilos! – but as we know, bigger isn’t always better when it comes to our bidders...
Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?
Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.
With their verdicts in, Monica and Marcus must make the final call. For some chefs, the critics’ reactions could strengthen their case; for others, they could expose the smallest weaknesses. With only three places in knockout week up for grabs, who has done enough to stay in the competition, and whose MasterChef journey ends here? programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
A healthy young labourer is found dead in a shallow ornamental pond on the vast country estate of Lady Philippa Armstrong and her son Jonathan. While the tragic incident initially appears to be nothing more than a straightforward workplace accident, Rose and Raj are called in to investigate glaring discrepancies. After all, how does a strong young man manage to drown in mere inches of water?
Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.
Struggling to navigate the complex social dynamics of the estate, Rose reluctantly accepts Joe’s persistent interference. Together, the duo soon uncover a dark web of deep-seated secrets and lies within the family and their devoted staff.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

In 1985, at the height of The Troubles, a Halloween-themed fancy-dress party in a local pub did something remarkable: it united a divided community. Forty years later, the small party that started as a fun distraction has grown into Europe’s largest Halloween festival, leaving the entire city spellbound.
We follow the ordinary people behind the extraordinary spectacle as they create and build the street theatre, costumes and art that bring Derry Halloween to life.
But this year isn’t without its own mischief and mayhem, from gale-force winds and structural collapses to wrangling a 50-metre snake.
Bringing together schools, youth clubs, dance troupes, workshops, costume makers and drumming bands, this is the story of a diverse city, young and old, dancing together in the streets, bound by a shared tradition, a fierce community spirit and an obsession with the dark arts of Halloween!

programme.title: Wild Horses, the Rockies and Me
programme.desc:
As summer comes to a close, wildlife film-maker Gordon Buchanan ventures deep into the epic majesty of Canada’s Rocky Mountains in search of one of nature’s most iconic animals: wild horses. Powerful, dangerous and elusive, wild horses are icons of the untamed west, yet they are surprisingly overlooked by science, and their lives remain largely undocumented. As a keen rider in his youth, Gordon aims to change that.
Set against the stunning peaks, open grasslands and shadowy pine forests that fringe the eastern slopes of the Rockies, Gordon rides out on his own steed hoping to get to places only a wild horse can reach. After a series of setbacks, he eventually finds a family of so-called wildies that consists of two competing stallions, two mares and their two young foals, and starts bearing witness to their behaviour. Which of the two stallions, Red or Crusoe, is the father of the foals, and who will earn the right to lead the band? What motivates Red to keep the band separated away from the super-herd that gathers each day? Would it not be wiser to join up with other horses to guard against ravenous grizzly bears and wolves looking to fatten up for winter? Will the innocence and curiosity of the two foals, Socks and Boots, get them into trouble?
To understand more about the horses, and in particular this unusual family, Gordon immerses himself further into their world, attempting to befriend them and hoping to earn their trust as he seeks to experience their lives from within a herd of wild horses, something that hasn’t been attempted before.
Gordon must move carefully and think like a wild horse. However, this is not without its dangers, as one well-placed kick could be fatal, meaning he must learn to read the subtle language of flicking ears, stamping hooves and quiet glances that reveal what the horses are telling each other about him, uncovering their complex intelligence and close family bonds.
As he begins to gain acceptance into the herd, Gordon discovers that they face a greater danger than wild predators: the threat of being culled. He realises the devastating impact this would have on family groups, as well as on the fragile ecosystems they help to shape.

The final is the ultimate test for the three remaining players as they perform a full concerto with a professional orchestra in front of a packed auditorium at Bristol Beacon. We follow their progress during rehearsals and find out exactly what it takes to perform at this level.
Accompanying our finalists is the BBC National Orchestra of Wales, with internationally renowned conductor Alpesh Chauhan. Petroc Trelawny brings us exclusive backstage access and full performances from the evening. Returning to the jury are our series judges, critically acclaimed pianist Joanna MacGregor and award-winning conductor Ben Gernon.
For the exciting finale, they are joined on the judging panel by celebrated composer and current Master of the King’s Music, Errollyn Wallen. Only they can decide who will be named BBC Young Musician 2026. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
An epic stretch of Scottish coastline is the first stop for Michael Portillo as he begins a series of coastal railway journeys around the British Isles.
Siccar Point, close to Dunbar on the Firth of Forth, was the site of an extraordinary 18th-century discovery and is today a place of pilgrimage for earth scientists from across the world. Michael finds out how James Hutton’s Unconformity upended biblical teaching about the age of the earth.
From North Berwick, Michael takes a boat a mile out into the Firth to visit one of the wildlife wonders of the world, a volcanic island known as Bass Rock. Long since abandoned by humans, it is now a breeding ground for 150,000 northern gannets. Standing with his seabird centre guide and with the white-and-yellow birds nesting and courting only feet away, Michael has to pinch himself to believe the scene.
Next stop is the Scottish capital, Edinburgh. Arriving at Britain’s second largest station, Waverley, Michael walks out into the Old Town with its castle and palace linked by the Royal Mile. He climbs to the city’s highest point, Arthur’s Seat, for a paleontologist’s story of settlement in the region from 7,000 years ago. Neither she nor Michael will forget the name of her favourite fossil, which is tattooed on her fingers.
At Holyrood House, the Queen’s official residence in Scotland, Michael visits the scene of a grisly 16th-century murder, which was the stuff of myth in his childhood. Mary Queen of Scots’ secretary, David Rizzio, was murdered by her husband and fellow lords in front of Mary in her private apartments. The palace building, its location and the historical events that took place within its walls help Michael to understand how royal power continues to be asserted in Scotland. programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
Michael Portillo continues his 300-mile Scottish coastal journey along the Firth of Forth at the railway engineering icon for which it is famous throughout the world – the Forth Bridge. A highlight for rail travellers, Michael remembers his delight in the crossing as a child visiting his Scottish grandparents.
On the firth’s southern bank, Michael stops in the port of Leith to tour the Royal Yacht Britannia. Now decommissioned, she is moored as an attraction. Michael is fascinated to hear how guests were entertained on board and is happy to recall an experience of his own concerning the fate of the world-famous vessel.
Heading west along the coast to Bo’ness, Michael savours the smuts puffing from the chimney of the Caledonian Blue locomotive belonging to the heritage Bo’ness and Kinneil Railway. The enthusiasm of the volunteers who run the line is infectious.
The next stop is in the Forth Valley close to Falkirk, where the Forth and Clyde Canal meets the River Carron and two 300-tonne steel sculptures tower over a vast eco-park. Michael is introduced to the Kelpies, Duke and Baron, by their creator, sculptor Andy Scott, who joins him on a video call from the United States.
Michael crosses the River Forth at Stirling, heading east to Alloa on the northern bank. One of Scotland’s oldest industries continues here today – glass manufacture. Michael tours a vast bottle-making plant staffed by generation upon generation of glass workers in a 270-year-old factory.
Travelling downstream to Culross, Michael discovers the railway - now freight only - runs along the waterfront because coastal strips of land such as this were flat and therefore relatively cheap. It cut the village from its foreshore. In Culross, Michael discovers a wonderfully preserved palace and recreated 16th-century garden. Presenter - Michael Portillo Director - Ben Rowland Series Editor - Alison Kreps Executive Producer - John Comerford Production Company - Fremantle.

Michael is struck by the emotional power these events retain seven centuries later.
Travelling across country to the River Tay, Michael discovers the fair city of Perth, the historic crowning place of the kings of Scotland. At Scone Palace, now the seat of the Earls of Mansfield, Michael meets William Murray, Viscount Stormont, who is the eldest son of the current Earl, to learn about the Stone of Scone, its seizure and return – ultimately – by the English.
As evening draws in, Michael heads for the banks of the Tay for a magical sunset canoe trip to spot beavers, who are now thriving here once again.
Kirkcaldy is Michael’s next stop, a station he knows well, having travelled here often to visit his Scottish grandparents in the town. Revisiting the beach where he played with his brothers, Michael meets a photographer who kindly takes a snap for the family album.
Tracking along the northern shores of the Firth of Forth, Michael admires the picturesque fishing villages. At St Monan’s, he discovers the old industry o salt-making is being revived, and it tastes good! programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn is John from Holywell, with a unique family heirloom – a detailed working model of a Welsh coal mine, built by his grandfather over 100 years ago. The model normally takes centre stage in the mining museum John runs, but the intricate mechanism that powered its moving parts was lost during a failed repair, and John’s pride and joy is currently out of service. Horologist Steve Fletcher faces the head-scratching challenge of recreating the entire mechanism, while art conservator Lucia Scalisi restores its painted surfaces, ensuring this miniature marvel honours John’s family history and the memory of generations of miners.
Next, Sarah and her daughter Laura arrive from Belfast, bringing along a tattered Victorian writing box steeped in family history. Originally gifted to Sarah’s grandmother Dolly by her fiance, it was later used by Sarah’s mum, Kay Kennedy, an inspirational reporter and one of Northern Ireland’s first female newspaper editors. Woodworker Will Kirk and bookbinder Chris Shaw join forces to restore the box’s battered veneer and torn leather, preserving its legacy for future generations, including Laura, who was inspired by Kay’s feats to become a writer and journalist herself.
From Barrow-in-Furness, Jacquie arrives with Rosebud – a 75-year-old doll that once belonged to her late mother, Myra, and became Myra’s treasured companion at a difficult time. After losing her father at the age of seven and her mother just two years later, Myra was adopted and given Rosebud by her new parents. Decades of loving and affection have left Rosebud with her head hanging loose, hair matted and missing, and lacking both her legs. Toy restorer Charlotte Abbott sets out to rebuild the missing limbs, secure the head and recreate Rosebud’s wig, returning this cherished doll to the family in one piece.
Finally, Tillie Newnham from Rugby presents an extraordinary piece of British engineering history: an original 1930s design for the Humber Bridge, drawn by Sir Ralph Freeman and later passed to her grandfather, Bernard Wex, who oversaw the bridge’s eventual construction.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc:
In the late 1980s, the British culinary scene was dominated by the traditions and techniques of French cuisine, and the kitchen hierarchy was rigid and unforgiving. Then, a working-class northerner with no interest in the rules became the most talked-about chef in the country. Marco Pierre White burst onto the scene and changed the future of British gastronomy, setting the standard that Gordon Ramsay and Heston Blumenthal would later be measured against.
The story begins with the opening of Harvey’s in 1987, the restaurant that made Marco's name. Contributors, including Marcus Wareing, Michel Roux Jr, Angela Hartnett, Clare Smyth and Tom Kerridge, reflect on what it meant to cook in the shadow of France and how Marco mastered the classical foundations before tearing up the rule book.
Into this world came a young Gordon Ramsay, hungry to learn and determined to prove himself. Under Marco's wing, he was tested to the limit. Gordon's remarkable stamina and his ability to learn quickly are explored, along with the stories that became kitchen legend, including falling asleep on the job during 18-hour shifts. Former colleagues and fellow chefs recall a driven newcomer who absorbed everything around him, and the bond, part mentorship and part rivalry, that took shape between teacher and pupil.
Meanwhile, a third force was emerging from a very different direction. Heston Blumenthal worked alongside Marco but shunned the traditional route to excellence, approaching cooking as a scientist might, asking why food behaves as it does and turning those answers into a fresh vision of what fine dining could achieve. His experimental mindset lifted the gastronomic experience to heights nobody had imagined and added a new dimension to the revolution already reshaping British cooking.
Set against the backdrop of the 'Cool Britannia' era of radical social and cultural change, the series explores a decade when fashion, politics and music were being torn up and rewritten. Another rock 'n' roll revolution was happening in the UK, this time in the kitchen. The story is one of rivalry and the pursuit of perfection, where the real heat was not just in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
Michael Portillo’s Scottish railway journey reaches Aberdeen. From the Granite City, Michael heads straight out to a dramatic piece of coastline 18 miles to its north. Forvie National Nature Reserve is 1000 hectares of protected coastal habitat dominated by grassy dunes. It’s a wild and fantastic landscape, and a perfect place to explore over and over again, since the dunes shift and change all the time.
Returning to Aberdeen, Michael finds out about the languages, dialects and vernacular of Scotland from a young ballad singer, who talks to him in Gaelic, Scots and Doric, and sings him a Scots ballad.
Dyce is Michael’s next stop. It’s the station for Aberdeen airport and the location for many businesses related to Scotland’s global energy industry. It’s an industry Michael knew well as a young special adviser to the energy secretary, and memories of flying out to oil and gas platforms remain with him. If there is an accident, training can make the difference between life and death. Michael is thrown in at the deep end, training for the terrifying scenario of a helicopter making a controlled descent into the sea.
The most easterly town in Scotland is Michael’s last port of call. At Peterhead, they land more fish than any other port in the United Kingdom. Michael is up early to see the traditional shout auction, where the catch is bought and sold, and to find out how the industry is coping after Brexit. Presenter - Michael Portillo Director - Ben Rowland Series Editor - Alison Kreps Executive Producer - John Comerford Production Company - Fremantle.

From whistling to her unborn calf to the first few hours of baby Samu's life and the struggles her eldest son faces leaving home, this film provides a rare insight into the lives of bottlenose dolphins. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Nine celebrities trace their family trees to explore the lives of their ancestors and uncover major themes in British social history.
Famous gardener Monty Don comes from a well-known dynasty of architects on his mother's side of the family but knows little about his other relatives.
He starts his investigation with a visit to his older brother David. Amongst the family memorabilia, they find a photograph of their great-grandmother Charlotte Wyatt, whose maiden name was Hodge. Monty is intrigued as no-one in the family has spoken much of the Hodges.
Monty's efforts lead him to a port near Anglesey, where he learns of extraordinary colonial travels and a national disaster that ended in a family tragedy.
On his father's side, Monty has heard that his ancestors were part of the famous Keiller marmalade dynasty, based in Dundee. Following their invention of chip marmalade, the Keillers became immensely rich, but Monty's immediate family saw none of the fortune. So where did the missing marmalade millions go?
Monty travels to Scotland to discover how his great-grandfather was involved in the business. He unearths a bitter family feud that finally answers his questions about the Keiller fortune. Director - Sarah Feltes Producer - Carrie Britton Participant - Monty Don.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there. Editor - Karen Wightman Executive Producer - Robin Barnwell Executive Producer - Darren Kemp Executive Producer - Tom Stone Producer - Gesbeen Mohammad Director - Gesbeen Mohammad.

programme.title: Sisters in Country: Dolly, Linda and Emmylou
programme.desc:
Documentary which explores how Dolly Parton, Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris's careers took off in the 1970s with very distinct takes on country before they ended up uniting as close harmony singers and eventually collaborated on 1987's four-million-selling debut album, Trio.
In the 60s, country music was viewed by most of America as blue collar, and Dolly was country through and through. Linda Ronstadt's take on classic country helped make her the biggest female star in mid-70s America. Folkie Emmylou learned about country from mentor Gram Parsons and, after his death in 1973, she became a bandleader in her own right. It was Emmylou and Linda - the two west coast folk rockers - who voiced their mutual appreciation of Dolly, the mountain girl singer from Tennessee, when they became early students of her work.
The artists talk about uniting as harmony singers and eventually collaborating on their debut album, Trio. The album helped launch the mountain music revival that would peak with the soundtrack to O Brother, Where Art Thou? In 2012, Linda Ronstadt was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, which left her unable to sing, but 2016 saw unreleased songs from their sessions compiled to create a third Trio album. This is the story of how their alliance made them pioneers in bringing different music worlds together and raising the game for women in the country tradition.
Contributors: Dolly Parton, Emmylou Harris, Linda Ronstadt, Rodney Crowell, George Lucas, Peter Asher, Chris Hillman, Laura Cantrell, Robert K Oermann, John Boylan, Phil Kaufman, David Lindley, Albert Lee, Herb Pedersen, George Massenberg and Applewood Road. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.desc:
Bridget is an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin care home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges late-night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely.
Into this secret world comes Paul, a vulnerable young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker. Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so he calls on his guardian angel - an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan. Bunny uses his personal history with the matron of Bridget’s nursing home to pull in a favour - a favour that will cost him dear. On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together, a mysterious comatose patient known only as ‘Anonymous’ wakes up and reveals he is a long-lost gangster with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. Could this treasure be the answer to all of Bridget and Paul’s troubles? Will they risk everything to find it?

programme.desc:
First to show his wares to Simon Bower and Nigel Havers is Philip, who has come up from Stoke with a stake, some holy water and all the other accoutrements any budding vampire killer would need. It’s an unusual collection, so which of the dealers will bite?
Next through the doors is Ben, with a rare coco de mer seed from a palm tree that only grows on two islands in the Seychelles. They’re one of the biggest seeds in the world – there's a record of one topping the scales at 25 kilos! – but as we know, bigger isn’t always better when it comes to our bidders...
Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?
Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.
With their verdicts in, Monica and Marcus must make the final call. For some chefs, the critics’ reactions could strengthen their case; for others, they could expose the smallest weaknesses. With only three places in knockout week up for grabs, who has done enough to stay in the competition, and whose MasterChef journey ends here? Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
A healthy young labourer is found dead in a shallow ornamental pond on the vast country estate of Lady Philippa Armstrong and her son Jonathan. While the tragic incident initially appears to be nothing more than a straightforward workplace accident, Rose and Raj are called in to investigate glaring discrepancies. After all, how does a strong young man manage to drown in mere inches of water?
Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.
Struggling to navigate the complex social dynamics of the estate, Rose reluctantly accepts Joe’s persistent interference. Together, the duo soon uncover a dark web of deep-seated secrets and lies within the family and their devoted staff.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.

Sticking with our gothic theme are Debbie and Alisha, with a pair of mourning brooches. They were incredibly popular in mid-19th-century Britain due to Queen Victoria's public mourning for Prince Albert. Such pieces have retained an enthusiastic following among collectors, so some strong offers are expected.
Fourth, and looking to trade childhood nostalgia for cold hard cash, is Heather, with a wind-up submarine toy. It hasn’t been underwater since she got it, so a demonstration for the dealers is a risky proposition. Will it sink or swim?
Last in is Paddy from Hartlepool, a town famous for the likely apocryphal tale that during the Napoleonic Wars, they hung a monkey after mistaking it for a French spy. Thankfully, there’s no simian espionage involved in Paddy’s sale today. Instead, he’s brought something both decorative and practical for today’s busy antique dealer - a clockwork spit roast. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for. Their next challenge is to prove that they can raise their game once again as they battle for one of just 12 places in knockout week. The competition is about to get serious.
First up, the chefs face the invention test. Under their mystery boxes on their benches is a surprise key ingredient that must take centre stage in their dish - coconut, an ingredient that can bring richness, sweetness and depth, but one that demands balance and precision to get right. The larder is packed with an impressive assortment of ingredients, from fish and chocolate to an array of pastry, giving the chefs endless possibilities to make the coconut sing.
But the challenge doesn’t end there. The chefs must cook for two of the country’s most discerning food critics, William Sitwell and Xanthe Clay, alongside new face, chef and writer Rahel Stephanie. Each chef must deliver their best two-course meal, showcasing originality and technical skill. With the standard higher than ever, every plate needs to make an impression.
With their verdicts in, Monica and Marcus must make the final call. For some chefs, the critics’ reactions could strengthen their case; for others, they could expose the smallest weaknesses. With only three places in knockout week up for grabs, who has done enough to stay in the competition, and whose MasterChef journey ends here? programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.sub-title: Introducing New Girl Band Rain and Shine ║ S5E5/7
programme.desc:
The Bowens, a family of five, call on Stacey and her team to transform their cluttered home in Wales. Mum-of-four Katrina recently moved her family from the West Midlands to start a new chapter in the countryside as a single parent. As a busy mum juggling everything on her own, Katrina struggles to find the time or space to tackle the chaos in her rented home.
With Stacey and the team’s help, the Bowens pack up every possession, stripping their home bare and revealing its hidden potential. During the packing process, we get to know the family behind the clutter as Stacey learns of 17-year-old Tayla’s childhood cancer diagnosis and recent remission.
Once packed, the family’s belongings are displayed in a vast warehouse – an awe-inspiring art installation of their lives, including 425 stuffed animals, 37 pairs of scissors and 123 fancy dress outfits. With everything displayed in front of them, the family are shocked to see how much they really own and wonder how it all fitted into their house in the first place. It’s a family effort to sort through all their belongings in just two days to reduce what they own by half.
There are emotional moments in the warehouse as Katrina reflects on the overwhelming period when she was pregnant with youngest daughter Olivia while Tayla was in hospital undergoing gruelling chemotherapy, as well as opening up about her recent separation from her husband and her hopes for a fresh start in their new home. With encouragement from her kids and best friend Andrea, she embraces letting go of the past and focusing on their future.
Finally, with the most treasured items carefully chosen, Stacey and the team race against the clock to complete the transformation. Rob builds a secret door to a cosy kids' den and revamps the family room into a welcoming space for everyone to enjoy. Iwan spring-cleans from top to bottom and creates a vibrant vegetable patch outside. Back in the house, Stacey sets the mission of bringing the calmness of the countryside indoors, while Dilly uses her organisational expertise to create practical solutions, giving Katrina more time to focus on herself and her children.
Will the Bowens' newly decluttered, stylish and functional home give them the fresh start they’ve been dreaming of?

Meanwhile, Joe overhears staff from Gallowbrae Hall discussing the suspicious death. Having spent much of his youth stealing from the estate, Joe knows the local personalities and the layout of the property inside out. Believing he can be of genuine help to an unconvinced Rose, he eagerly inserts himself straight into the investigation. Finding themselves reluctantly paired up once again, Rose and Joe must untangle the messy, tight-knit relationships of Gallowbrae’s eccentric inhabitants.
At the centre of the drama are the Armstrongs, an old-money family desperately holding onto what’s theirs while caught in a fierce controversy over a new rewilding scheme. This scheme will close off public land to reintroduce sensitive wildlife and plants, sparking intense outrage from one local inhabitant in particular. Adding to the tension are Maxine, the devastated housekeeper who keeps her cards close to her chest; Whittick, the grouchy gamekeeper fiercely determined to protect Gallowbrae at any cost; and Gavin, the angry intruder and conspiracy theorist who views the aristocratic family and everything they stand for as completely abhorrent.
Struggling to navigate the complex social dynamics of the estate, Rose reluctantly accepts Joe’s persistent interference. Together, the duo soon uncover a dark web of deep-seated secrets and lies within the family and their devoted staff.

It is a forest full of secrets, with a vast watery underworld that is still being explored and which holds the key to how animals and people survive the dry season. Eliud Porras - Narrator.

programme.title: Mexico: Earth's Festival of Life
programme.desc: In the deserts of northern Mexico life has found clever ways to survive against the odds. Prairie dogs fight snakes, bats hunt scorpions and tiny owls live in giant cacti. Eliud Porras - Narrator.

programme.title: Mexico: Earth's Festival of Life
programme.desc: Mexico is a vast country, over two thousand miles long, dominated by a great chain of mountains, the Sierra Madre. Journey down this rocky spine and you'll discover an amazing diversity of life, from black bears and orchid bees to resplendent quetzals and millions of monarch butterflies. This is a land where giant volcanoes simmer and ancient and modern cultures collide in a festival of life. Eliud Porras - Narrator.

programme.sub-title: S2E7 ║ Whitby to Robin Hood's Bay ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2023
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his railway adventure at Whitby, where he explores the port's shipbuilding and seafaring heritage. In Grosmont, Michael boards the first steam locomotive built in Britain since the 1960s. In the vast open landscape of the North York Moors, Michael discovers one of the most powerful military radars in the world - where tension rises as the team suspect a missile launch. Ben Rowland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: The World at War
programme.sub-title: S1E14 ║ It's A Lovely Day Tomorrow ║ Documentary / War / History ║ 1974

programme.title: World at War

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E1 ║ Warrington to Preston ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Armed with his early 20th century Bradshaw's Guide, Michael Portillo embarks on a journey through Britain's industrial heartland in the footsteps of King George V. He starts in Warrington and learns how the mayor, Dr George Joseph, received the royal party in the parlour of Warrington's magnificent town hall. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E3 ║ Manchester to Elsecar ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: In Manchester at the magnificent Heaton Park, Michael discovers one of the first open air concerts was held here in 1909 by an opera fan, William Grimshaw, who entertained 40,000 people to the music of opera superstar, Enrico Caruso, on a gramophone. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E4 ║ Maltby to Hinckley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael heads for Maltby, where he is caught up with the thrill of the chase as he investigates the high-octane sport of whippet racing. He learns how this `poor man's sport' grew during the 19th century in the mining towns of the north and retains its appeal today. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E5 ║ Birmingham to the Potteries ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches Birmingham and discovers how a radical reformer would make his mark on the city of a thousand trades. At Highbury Hall he finds Joseph Chamberlain's splendid mansion home and hears how he established a political dynasty including a Prime Minister and a Foreign Secretary. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E2 ║ Blackburn to Manchester ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: In Blackburn Michael catches a rare glimpse of Edwardian life on celluloid and marvels at how factory workers and schoolchildren alike were drawn to seek fame on film. Continuing east to Nelson, Michael braves the enemy camp to have a pint of tea with the socialist working classes in Britain's last Clarion House. Way out of his comfort zone, he is heartened by their warm welcome. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Early 20th century Britain was reeling from industrial strife and suffragette outrages but the biggest crisis of all was the conflict in Ireland. Beginning in Newry, Michael finds a specially chartered train would deliver demonstrators campaigning for Irish Home Rule to a rally in the town. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

Their ambition for the house is enormous, as Kara wants to create a home that is not only beautiful but will help her regain some independence. With money tight, Jonny needs to take on a lot of the work himself. As the build progresses, and despite the challenges coming thick and fast, compromise is not an option with both form and function so essential.
